Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround and for prepping the prompts. A few concrete suggestions from the Redwood eval team so we get useful, comparable results: 

1) What to send: please include both raw transcripts and a redacted copy for a ~20% sample set. Raw helps us characterize model behavior; redacted helps validate your compliance process. If raw sharing isn't possible, the redacted sample is sufficient to start.

2) Edge cases to prioritize: 
   - Very long customer transcripts (> 7k chars) to stress KV cache and memory behavior
   - Rapid turn-by-turn multi-user chats (overlapping speakers)
   - Non-English or code-switched segments (English + Spanish)
   - Explicit content and obfuscated PII (e.g., 'john [at] example dot com')

3) Redaction guidance: 
   - Replace direct identifiers with consistent placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL_REDACTED>, <SSN_REDACTED>), and keep a separate mapping document locally — do not include mapping in uploads.
   - For names that are critical to context (e.g., agent vs. customer role), prefer role labels (AGENT / CUSTOMER) rather than real names.

4) Initial model recommendations for evaluation (fast iteration):
   - redwood-13b-opt (8-bit quant) — good balance of cost and quality for summarization tasks
   - redwood-33b-pt (16-bit) — higher quality for edge cases, useful for regression checks
   - For a low-cost baseline: open-7b-quant (if you want to compare an open baseline)

5) Benchmarks / eval dashboards: we'll run a focused quality eval (ROUGE + custom relevance metrics) and a latency/cost profile. Results will be published to the eval dashboard linked here: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/ACME-123. We'll also attach a short PDF with sample outputs and our redaction validation protocol.

6) Timeline: if you upload prompts by Tuesday EOD, we can return an initial model-fit report and prioritized next steps by Friday. If you need NDAs or upload-only links, let me know and I can get that arranged.

Ben — for latency sizing, the P95 350ms target is aggressive for long transcripts; recommend we start tests at 100 concurrent requests and scale from there. Can you prepare a Dedicated sizing estimate if we hit the SLA target during the eval?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
